YOUR COMMUNITY. YOUR CODE.

Meet chatbox.js

Give your community a bot with personality.
One import for messages, embeds, DMs, and moderation. Choose a hosting guide below.

Node.js 20.3+No dependenciesES modules

Dashboard hosting

Open the Developer Portal, select your application, then Hosting Open Bot Studio. Upload a JavaScript file or type in the editor. It includes highlighting, line numbers, and autocomplete. Save draft saves your work without changing the running bot. Publish & run 24/7 activates it. You can close your browser; Supabase handles new messages for you.

Hosted bot · no token needed 
import { Client, Events, EmbedBuilder } from 'chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.content === '!ping') await message.reply('Pong!');
  if (message.content === '!dm') await message.author.send('Hello!');
});
await client.login();

Hosted bots receive new human messages in channels and DMs they can access. Bot messages do not trigger other hosted bots, preventing reply loops. Your published script starts fresh for each event. Replies, embeds, DMs, word matching, and authorized moderation use the same API as self-hosted bots.

Execution limits: each event gets 8 API calls, 8 MB of JavaScript memory, approximately 150 ms of script CPU time, and an 8-second deadline. Scripts can be up to 80,000 characters. Only chatbox.js can be imported. External fetch, npm packages, timers, persistent global variables, and startup events require the Node.js option below. A failed event is logged and is not automatically replayed, avoiding duplicate replies or moderation actions.

Logs: refresh Recent executions to see the last 20 runs. Logs are retained for 7 days. Stop hosting pauses future events; an API action already in progress may finish. Publishing a new version cancels pending events from the old version.

Hosting stays available without an open dashboard and wakes on messages instead of polling channel history. Queued work has a once-per-minute recovery check. Backlogs can take longer to process. Availability and usage still follow your Supabase project's quotas.

To switch to your own host, download your script and chatbox.js, then set your bot token as shown below. Stop dashboard hosting before starting the same bot elsewhere to avoid duplicate replies.

Self-hosting with Node.js

Create a bot in Server settings Apps & Bots. Save its token in your environment. Run your bot with Node.js 20.3 or newer on your computer or a server.

GitHub Pages hosts the chat UI and this guide. With this option, your bot is a separate Node process. Dashboard hosting above is also available.

1. Download three files

chatbox.js example-bot.mjs package.json

Put them in the same folder. The package file contains "type": "module". No npm dependencies are required. This is a local SDK download, not an npm package named chatbox.js.

2. Set your token and run

PowerShell 
$env:CHATBOX_BOT_TOKEN = "your-bot-token"
node example-bot.mjs

Send !ping, !embed, or !dm in a channel the bot can see.

3. Your first bot

JavaScript 
import { Client, Events, EmbedBuilder, Colors } from './chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
client.once(Events.ClientReady, () => console.log(`Ready as ${client.user.displayName}`));
client.on(Events.Error, error => console.error(error.message));
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot) return;
  if (message.content === '!ping') await message.reply('Pong!');
  if (message.content === '!embed') {
    const embed = new EmbedBuilder().setColor(Colors.Blurple)
      .setTitle('Hello from CHATBOX').setDescription('One import. Your own bot.')
      .addFields({name:'Commands',value:'`!ping` · `!embed` · `!dm`'})
      .setFooter({text:'Built with chatbox.js'}).setTimestamp();
    await message.reply({embeds:[embed]});
  }
  if (message.content === '!dm') await message.author.send('You asked for a DM. Here it is!');
});
process.once('SIGINT', () => client.destroy());
await client.login();

4. Keep it running

The bot runs while the Node.js process and its computer or server stay online. Closing the terminal or shutting down the host stops it. For 24/7 operation, use an always-on server and its process manager or service system. Restart the process after editing your script. Stop dashboard hosting before running the same bot here to avoid duplicate replies.

Cloudflare hosting

Run a scheduled Worker in your own Cloudflare account, with a Durable Object to keep the bot’s message cursor. This uses the same CHATBOX database and SDK.

1. Download the files

Create an empty folder for this bot. Save these three files together. Rename cloudflare-wrangler.jsonc to wrangler.jsonc.

chatbox.jscloudflare-worker.mjswrangler.jsonc

Use a current Node.js LTS release and your own Cloudflare account. This guide does not require exporting or moving your CHATBOX database. Check your Cloudflare plan's Workers and Durable Objects limits before deploying.

2. Install Wrangler and sign in

Terminal · in your bot folder 
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev wrangler
npx wrangler login

Open wrangler.jsonc and change name to a unique Worker name. Keep nodejs_compat: chatbox.js uses Node's EventEmitter. The configuration creates a SQLite-backed Durable Object and a once-per-minute schedule. No KV namespace IDs need to be copied.

In CHATBOX, open Server settings Apps & Bots. Create a bot and copy its token. Give it access only to the channels it needs. Stop Bot Studio hosting if this is the same bot you previously hosted there.

3. Add the secret and deploy

Terminal 
npx wrangler deploy
npx wrangler secret put CHATBOX_BOT_TOKEN
npx wrangler types

Paste the bot token into Wrangler's secret prompt. Never put it in source code, a public repository, or wrangler.jsonc. If a scheduled run happens before the secret is set, it fails without sending messages; the next run will try again.

The default example replies to !ping and !embed. Edit its Events.MessageCreate handler to add your commands, then run npx wrangler deploy again. Keep the scheduled entry point and poll: false setting; a Worker does not run a permanent Node polling loop.

4. Verify your bot

Allow the schedule to initialize, then send !ping in a channel your bot can read and send to. Responses normally arrive on the next minute's run; new cron schedules can take several minutes to propagate.

Live logs 
npx wrangler tail

Look for chatbox.batch and a processed count. An initial count of zero is normal: the bot starts at the current server time instead of replaying old messages. If it cannot reply, check its channel permissions, slowmode, AutoMod, token, and Supabase availability.

To pause it, remove the cron entry from the config and deploy again. To revoke its access immediately, revoke the bot token in CHATBOX. A public request to the Worker URL only displays a status message; it cannot trigger a bot run.

What this example does

Cloudflare calls the scheduled handler once a minute. One Durable Object prevents overlapping batches and stores the last message cursor. Each run handles at most 25 events. A busy channel can build a backlog; adjust maxEvents only after considering API and runtime limits.

The cursor is saved before each handler runs. A crash or failed action can skip that event, but the example will not replay it automatically and duplicate a reply or moderation action. It is an at-most-once example, not an exactly-once job system.

This host checks the API even while chat is idle. Dashboard hosting on Supabase wakes on new messages and avoids that idle polling. Use the option that suits your bot. Both hosts enforce the same CHATBOX permissions and moderation rules.

Official references: Cron triggers, secrets, Node compatibility, and Durable Object namespaces.

Button callbacks & ephemeral replies

Send buttons with a unique custom_id, then handle clicks in Events.InteractionCreate. Your callback runs on the bot host. Use ephemeral: true to reply only to the member who clicked; leave it out for a public channel reply.

Try the button styles Local preview — no bot or message is sent.

Link

Only you can see this ·
Style Appearance Behavior
ButtonStyle.Primary Blurple Click callback
ButtonStyle.Secondary Gray Click callback
ButtonStyle.Success Green Click callback
ButtonStyle.Danger Red Click callback; the label alone never deletes anything
ButtonStyle.Link Gray with an arrow Opens an HTTPS URL; no callback
Hosted bot · buttons and private callbacks 
import { Client, Events, ButtonBuilder, ButtonStyle,
  ActionRowBuilder } from 'chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();

client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot || message.content !== '!buttons') return;
  const row = new ActionRowBuilder().addComponents(
    new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId('help').setLabel('Help')
      .setStyle(ButtonStyle.Primary),
    new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId('details').setLabel('Details')
      .setStyle(ButtonStyle.Secondary),
    new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId('confirm').setLabel('Confirm')
      .setStyle(ButtonStyle.Success),
    new ButtonBuilder().setCustomId('cancel').setLabel('Cancel')
      .setStyle(ButtonStyle.Danger),
    new ButtonBuilder().setLabel('Guide').setStyle(ButtonStyle.Link)
      .setURL('https://ipmingsum2.github.io/external/chatbox/index.html')
  );
  await message.reply({ content: 'Choose an action:', components: [row] });
});

// Map each button ID to its callback. Keep handlers registered on every run.
const callbacks = {
  help: () => 'How can I help?',
  details: () => 'These details are only visible to you.',
  confirm: () => 'You confirmed!',
  cancel: () => 'Cancelled. Nothing was deleted.'
};
client.on(Events.InteractionCreate, async interaction => {
  if (!interaction.isButton()) return;
  const callback = callbacks[interaction.customId];
  if (!callback) return;
  await interaction.reply({
    content: await callback(interaction),
    ephemeral: true
  });
});
await client.login();

Upload this example to Bot Studio, publish it, and send !buttons. For Node.js or Workers, import ./chatbox.js and log in with your bot token. Buttons work in channels and bot DMs. Use .setDisabled(true) to disable a button. Callback functions stay in your script; only button IDs travel with messages.

Private means only the requesting member

Ephemeral replies support text and embeds. They appear in a private response dialog, not channel history, and other members cannot fetch the response. They work with button clicks, slash commands, and form submissions. Use interaction.reply({ content: 'Done', ephemeral: true }); channel.send() and ordinary message replies are public. Each interaction accepts one response within 15 minutes. Private reply buttons, follow-up replies, and editing a private reply are not supported yet.

Your application, in its own space

Open the Developer Portal . Sign in with your CHATBOX account. Administrators can create applications; owners manage their applications and root can manage all of them.

  • General information: change the bot username, display name, description, status, avatar, banner image, and banner color. Upload PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or AVIF images up to 4 MB, or use HTTPS image URLs.
  • Bot & token: create, reset or revoke a token with server-verified hCaptcha. A new token is shown once. Resetting invalidates the previous token immediately.
  • Commands: inspect registered definitions. Register and update them through the API in your script.
  • Hosting: upload/write JavaScript in Bot Studio for 24/7 execution, or follow the Node.js and Cloudflare sections on this page.
  • Permissions: root grants API scopes. Bots cannot assign staff roles, change passwords, or delete user accounts.
Bot identity API 
await client.user.setUsername('orbit_bot');
await client.user.setAvatar('https://example.com/avatar.png');
await client.user.setBanner('https://example.com/banner.png');
await client.application.edit({ description: 'Your helpful community bot' });
await client.profile.edit({ display_name: 'Orbit', status: 'Ready to help',
  banner_color: '#7867ed' });

Switch CHATBOX accounts

Open User Settings Switch accounts or the portal’s Switch accounts button. Add another account with email, password and hCaptcha, then switch without signing in again. Remove inactive accounts with the Remove button. Log Out signs out the active account only.

Sessions are saved on this device, like the existing Supabase sign-in session; passwords are never saved. Anyone with access to this browser profile can switch saved accounts. Switching reloads the page to clear the previous account’s cached data and subscriptions. Expired or revoked sessions require sign-in again.

Slash commands with real arguments

Define commands with SlashCommandBuilder, then register them with client.commands.set(). CHATBOX generates named inputs and selectors from the schema. The server validates the values, choices, references, required fields, and limits before the bot receives the interaction.

Download a complete typed-command and autocomplete bot. Use it on Node.js, or change the import to 'chatbox.js' for dashboard hosting.

Register and handle /purge count 
import { Client, Events, SlashCommandBuilder } from 'chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
const purge = new SlashCommandBuilder().setName('purge')
  .setDescription('Remove recent messages')
  .setRequiredRole('Moderator') // CHATBOX: enforced on the invoking member.
  .addIntegerOption(o => o.setName('count').setDescription('How many?')
    .setRequired(true).setMinValue(1).setMaxValue(100));
client.once(Events.ClientReady, async () => {
  await client.commands.set([purge]);
});
client.on(Events.InteractionCreate, async interaction => {
  if (!interaction.isChatInputCommand() || interaction.commandName !== 'purge') return;
  const count = interaction.options.getInteger('count', true);
  const deleted = await interaction.channel.bulkDelete(count);
  await interaction.reply({ content: `Removed ${deleted.size} messages.`, ephemeral: true });
});
await client.login();

Root must grant this bot manage_messages and the owner must remain Moderator or higher. setRequiredRole() restricts who can run the command. Without it, a command is available to members who can send in its channel, so check the invoking member before performing privileged operations.

Argument Builder method Interaction getter
String addStringOption getString
Integer addIntegerOption getInteger
Boolean addBooleanOption getBoolean
User addUserOption getUser / getMember
Channel or category addChannelOption getChannel
Role addRoleOption getRole
User or role addMentionableOption getMentionable
Decimal number addNumberOption getNumber
File attachment addAttachmentOption getAttachment
Subcommand addSubcommand getSubcommand
Subcommand group addSubcommandGroup getSubcommandGroup

These correspond to Discord’s argument types. CHATBOX references its own users, roles, channels and files. Voice channels, Discord IDs, localization, OAuth installations and Discord permission bitfields do not exist here. Command and argument names use lowercase letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens.

Choices, limits and nested commands

Builder options 
const tools = new SlashCommandBuilder().setName('tools').setDescription('Tools')
  .addSubcommandGroup(group => group.setName('profile').setDescription('Profiles')
    .addSubcommand(sub => sub.setName('inspect').setDescription('Inspect a member')
      .addUserOption(o => o.setName('member').setDescription('Who?').setRequired(true))
      .addStringOption(o => o.setName('detail').setDescription('Detail level')
        .addChoices({name:'Short',value:'short'}, {name:'Full',value:'full'}))));
// Inside the handler:
const group = interaction.options.getSubcommandGroup(); // 'profile'
const sub = interaction.options.getSubcommand(); // 'inspect'
const member = interaction.options.getUser('member', true); // User with send()/createDM()
const detail = interaction.options.getString('detail') ?? 'short';

Use setMinValue/setMaxValue for numbers, setMinLength/setMaxLength for strings, addChannelTypes(ChannelType.GuildText, ChannelType.GuildCategory) for channels, and setFileTypes('image', '.pdf') for attachments. Required arguments come before optional ones. Use up to 25 options per level, 25 choices per option, and 100 commands per bot. Nest groups subcommands arguments; do not mix subcommands with ordinary arguments at the same level.

CHATBOX custom inputs

More than plain text 
const reminder = new SlashCommandBuilder().setName('reminder').setDescription('Capture details')
  .addDurationOption(o => o.setName('wait').setDescription('For example 5m or 2h'))
  .addDateOption(o => o.setName('day').setDescription('Calendar date'))
  .addColorOption(o => o.setName('color').setDescription('Hex color'))
  .addMultilineOption(o => o.setName('note').setDescription('Longer note').setMaxLength(1000))
  .addURLOption(o => o.setName('link').setDescription('HTTPS link'));
// These are string options with a server-checked CHATBOX format.
const seconds = interaction.options.getDuration('wait'); // '5m'  300
const date = interaction.options.getDate('day'); // Date at midnight UTC
const color = interaction.options.getColor('color'); // '#5865f2'  integer
const note = interaction.options.getString('note');
const file = interaction.options.getAttachment('file');
if (file) console.log(await file.getURL()); // Authorized download link, valid for 5 minutes.

Duration units: s, m, h, d, w. Date uses YYYY-MM-DD. Colors use #RRGGBB. Attachment uploads stay private to their channel; the API authorizes a short-lived download URL. A form does not schedule work by itself: timers or persistent scheduling need your host’s implementation.

Dynamic autocomplete callbacks

App-provided suggestions 
const search = new SlashCommandBuilder().setName('search').setDescription('Search topics')
  .addStringOption(o => o.setName('topic').setDescription('Topic')
    .setRequired(true).setAutocomplete(true));
client.on(Events.InteractionCreate, async interaction => {
  if (!interaction.isAutocomplete()) return;
  const prefix = String(interaction.options.getFocused()).toLowerCase();
  await interaction.respond(['Luau', 'JavaScript', 'TypeScript']
    .filter(name => name.toLowerCase().includes(prefix))
    .map(name => ({name, value:name})));
});

Autocomplete supports string, integer and number options; use it instead of fixed choices. It is debounced in chat, private to the requesting member and limited to 25 results. Keep callbacks fast. A once-per-minute Worker may respond too slowly for live autocomplete; use dashboard hosting or a continuously running Node process. Typed values still pass full validation on submission.

client.commands.create(builder), edit(name, builder), delete(name), and fetch(name?) manage one command at a time. set([...]) replaces the whole list. Registration is idempotent when definitions are unchanged. Hosted ClientReady runs on publish/startup; regular message executions do not register commands again.

Bulk deletion, pins & reactions

Message management API 
const channel = await client.channels.fetch(channelId);
const recent = await channel.messages.fetch({limit:25}); // Newest first, returns an array.
const older = await channel.messages.fetch({limit:25, before:recent.at(-1).id});
const newer = await channel.messages.fetch({afterId:recent[0].id, limit:25});
const message = await channel.messages.fetch(messageId); // One Message.
await message.pin();
await message.unpin();
await message.react('👍');
const reactions = await message.reactions.fetch(); // [{emoji, count, me}]
await message.reactions.remove('👍'); // Remove this bot’s reaction.
await message.reactions.removeAll(); // Requires manage_messages.
const pins = await channel.messages.fetchPinned();
const deleted = await channel.bulkDelete(20); // One API call, 1–100 recent messages.
// Or use IDs, an array of Message objects, or a Collection:
const removed = await channel.bulkDelete([messageId, anotherMessageId]);
console.log(removed.size); // Collection of the IDs removed.

Bulk deletion is atomic and restricted to one visible channel. It removes content, attachments, embeds, components, pins and reactions from the selected conversation messages. No “message deleted” placeholder appears in chat. Already deleted IDs are not counted again. CHATBOX keeps its internal deletion markers for synchronization and has no Discord two-week age restriction.

A bot can delete its own messages. Deleting other members’ messages, pinning, or clearing all reactions requires manage_messages and a Moderator-or-higher owner. Timeouts prevent writes. Private-channel checks apply to fetches, cursors, pins, reactions and attachment links.

REST routes include POST /v1/channels/{id}/messages/bulk-delete with {messages:[id1,id2]} or {count:20}, GET /v1/channels/{id}/pins, GET /v1/messages/{id}, and GET|PUT|POST /v1/commands. Command updates/deletes use PATCH|DELETE /v1/commands/{name}. Pins/reactions and other SDK actions also work through POST /v1/actions.

Buttons, commands & forms

Apps can open a custom form from a message button or a slash command. The form identifies the receiving bot. Submissions go only to that bot; an ephemeral reply is visible only to the submitting member.

Download a complete application-form bot. Upload it in Bot Studio and publish. The script registers its commands through the API on startup. Type /apply in chat, or send !apply to get a button.

Form handler 
import { Client, Events, ModalBuilder, TextInputBuilder,
  ActionRowBuilder, TextInputStyle } from 'chatbox.js';
const client = new Client();
client.on(Events.InteractionCreate, async interaction => {
  if (interaction.isChatInputCommand() && interaction.commandName === 'apply') {
    await interaction.showModal(new ModalBuilder()
      .setCustomId('application').setTitle('Access request')
      .addComponents(new ActionRowBuilder().addComponents(
        new TextInputBuilder().setCustomId('reason')
          .setLabel('Why would you like access?')
          .setStyle(TextInputStyle.Paragraph).setMaxLength(1000)
      )));
  } else if (interaction.isModalSubmit()) {
    const reason = interaction.fields.getTextInputValue('reason');
    await interaction.reply({content: 'Thanks for your response!', ephemeral: true});
  }
});
await client.login();

For Node.js or Workers, import ./chatbox.js. Register commands once with await client.commands.set([{name:'apply',description:'Open an application form'}]) in a ClientReady handler. Registration replaces that bot’s command list. Hosted publishing queues a startup event; no manual command menu is needed.

Commands declare typed named arguments through the command API. Older commands without an argument schema retain getString('input') for compatibility. Buttons use ButtonBuilder, ButtonStyle, and ActionRowBuilder; send rows in the message’s components array. Link buttons require HTTPS.

Forms support 1–5 text fields, required/optional fields, placeholders, short/paragraph styles and maximum lengths. Each interaction can be answered once within 15 minutes. The chat waits up to 90 seconds; keep handlers short. Hosted bots receive events immediately when capacity allows; Workers cron normally adds up to one minute of latency. Self-hosted polling claims interactions once, so failed handlers are not automatically replayed.

Manage your community

These methods work in hosted and self-hosted bots. Channel access, AutoMod, slowmode, timeouts and role hierarchy remain enforced by the server.

Common operations 
await client.profile.edit({display_name:'Helper',bio:'Here to help.'});
const members = await client.members.fetch();
const roles = await client.roles.fetch(); // Read only: only root assigns roles.
await client.members.setNickname(userId, 'New nickname');
const history = await client.members.standing(userId);
const created = await client.channels.create({name:'projects',is_private:true});
await client.channels.edit(created.id, {slowmode_seconds:10});
await client.channels.setPermission({channel_id:created.id,
  subject:'user:' + userId,permission:'view',value:true});
await client.channels.archive(created.id);
await client.categories.create({name:'Projects',sort_order:2});
const categories = await client.categories.fetch();
await client.categories.delete(categoryId); // Channels are preserved.
const thread = await client.threads.create({channel_id:channelId,name:'Ideas'});
await client.threads.archive({id:thread.id,archived:true});
const poll = await client.polls.create({channel_id:channelId,question:'Which day?',
  answers:[{text:'Saturday'},{text:'Sunday'}],duration_hours:24,multiple:false});
const [results] = await client.polls.fetch(channelId,[poll.id]);
await client.polls.vote({id:poll.id,choices:[results.options[0].id]});
await client.polls.close(poll.id);

Root must explicitly grant manage_channels for channels/categories and manage_members for nicknames. The bot owner must also be an Administrator or higher for channel management, or Moderator or higher for nicknames. Moderation history requires moderate. No bot can assign staff roles.

The generic endpoint POST /v1/actions accepts {action,payload} and the same Authorization: Bot … header. It uses the same permission checks as SDK methods; it does not expose arbitrary SQL or administrator credentials.

CHATBOX has no voice/video gateway, Discord servers, Discord OAuth, billing, external app installation, or Discord moderation infrastructure. Those Discord APIs cannot be provided by this app. Components currently support buttons and text-input forms. Message component select menus and follow-up interaction webhooks are not implemented.

02

Messages & events

messageCreate gives you a message with content, author, channel, channelId, embeds, id, and createdTimestamp. Ignore bot authors to avoid reply loops.

JavaScript 
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot) return;
  if (message.content === '!hello') {
    const sent = await message.reply('Hello!');
    await sent.edit('Hello, everyone!');
    // await sent.delete();
  }
});

// Send to a known channel ID (the ID is in the chat URL hash).
const channel = await client.channels.fetch('YOUR_CHANNEL_ID');
await channel.send('A new update is ready.');
How events work: one HTTP poll checks all channels the bot may view, normally every 3 seconds. This is not Discord’s WebSocket Gateway. New messages are delivered; edit/delete events, typing, presence, voice, and reaction events are not implemented. Slash commands, buttons, and form submissions use Events.InteractionCreate; see Buttons & ephemeral replies Buttons, commands & forms.

Use client.once(Events.ClientReady, handler), client.on(Events.Error, handler), and client.destroy() to manage the process. Channel fetch returns a Map when no ID is provided.

03

Rich embeds

Use EmbedBuilder for colored cards with a title, Markdown description, fields, author, footer, timestamp, thumbnail, and image. The same embed renderer works in channels, threads, and DMs.

Orbit APP

Weekend build night

Bring an idea. We’ll build it together.

When

Saturday, 8 PM

Where

#dev-talk

Community events · Today
JavaScript 
const embed = new EmbedBuilder()
  .setColor(Colors.Blurple)
  .setAuthor({ name: 'Orbit' })
  .setTitle('Weekend build night')
  .setURL('https://ipmingsum2.github.io/external/chat.html')
  .setDescription('Bring an idea. We’ll build it **together**.')
  .addFields(
    { name: 'When', value: 'Saturday, 8 PM', inline: true },
    { name: 'Where', value: '#dev-talk', inline: true }
  )
  .setFooter({ text: 'Community events' })
  .setTimestamp();
await channel.send({ content: 'You’re invited!', embeds: [embed] });
// Optional: .setImage('https://...') or .setThumbnail('https://...')

Use HTTPS for links and images. Limits: 10 embeds per message; 25 fields per embed; title 256 characters; description 4096; field name 256; field value 1024; footer 2048; combined embed text and URLs 6000. AutoMod checks embed content too. Raw HTML is not supported.

04

Direct messages

Bots can open a DM with a member and send text or embeds. A bot only sees DMs it participates in; it cannot inspect conversations between other people.

JavaScript 
const user = await client.users.fetch('MEMBER_UUID');
await user.send('Hello! Here is the update you requested.');

// Or respond privately to someone who asks:
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (!message.author.bot && message.content === '!helpme') {
    await message.author.send({ embeds: [
      new EmbedBuilder().setTitle('Help').setDescription('How can I help?')
    ] });
  }
});

DM creation is limited to 10 requests per minute per bot. Reopening the same conversation returns the same channel. Sending still follows message rate limits and AutoMod.

05

Moderation

Messaging works by default. Root can grant optional permissions in Apps & Bots Permissions. Bots never receive human staff roles and cannot moderate staff or root.

Permission Allows
moderate Warn, mute, ban, unban, remove mute. The bot owner must still be Moderator or higher.
manage_messages Delete another member’s message in a channel the bot can view. AutoMod system alerts are protected.
automod Create, edit, and delete AutoMod rules. The owner must still be Administrator or higher.
JavaScript 
await client.moderation.warn(userId, 'Please follow the rules.', 'Message evidence');
await client.moderation.timeout(userId, 600, 'Repeated spam'); // seconds
await client.moderation.untimeout(userId, 'Appeal accepted');
await client.moderation.ban(userId, 'Spam', { seconds: 86400 });
await client.moderation.unban(userId, 'Appeal accepted');
// Omit seconds for a permanent ban. All actions require a reason.

Moderation actions are recorded in Account Standing. A revoked token or permission takes effect on subsequent requests. Bots under a warning, ban, or timeout cannot bypass their restriction.

06

Words, wildcards & AutoMod

Separate plain phrases with commas or new lines. Matching is case-insensitive. * matches additional characters within a word. Regex patterns are separate and stay one per line, so commas inside regex are preserved.

Keyword Matches Does not match
cat cat, cat! cats, bobcat
cat* cat, cats, caterpillar bobcat
*cat cat, bobcat cats
*cat* cats, bobcats dog

Detect words in your Node bot

JavaScript 
import { matchesWords } from './chatbox.js';
client.on(Events.MessageCreate, async message => {
  if (message.author.bot) return;
  if (matchesWords(message.content, ['spam*, unwanted phrase'], {
    allowedWords: ['spamton'], patterns: [/repeat\d+/i]
  })) {
    // Requires root-granted moderate permission.
    await client.moderation.warn(message.author.id, 'Please rephrase.', message.content);
  }
});

Bot handlers see messages after they are posted. Use server AutoMod to block content before it appears.

Configure server AutoMod

JavaScript 
await client.automod.save({
  id: 'my-bot-spam-rule', name: 'Spam phrases', enabled: true,
  words: ['spam*, unwanted phrase'], allowed_words: ['spamton'],
  patterns: ['repeat[0-9]+'], // PostgreSQL regex, not JavaScript RegExp
  block_message: 'Please keep the conversation on topic.',
  actions: ['warning', 'timeout'], timeout_seconds: 600,
  log_channel_id: 'PRIVATE_LOG_CHANNEL_ID'
});
await client.automod.delete('my-bot-spam-rule');

Rules always block matches. Optional actions are warning, timeout, and ban. Use ban_seconds for a temporary ban, or null for permanent. Omit the log channel to keep events staff-only. Plain keywords follow Discord’s wildcard approach; the regex engine here is PostgreSQL.

07

API reference

SDK Purpose
client.login(token?) Authenticate and start new-message polling
client.channels.fetch(id?) Fetch one channel or all visible channels
channel.send(string | {content, embeds}) Send a message
channel.messages.fetch({after, afterId}) Read up to 100 messages after a cursor
message.reply / edit / delete Reply, update your own message, or delete
client.users.fetch(id) Fetch a member profile
user.send(payload) / user.createDM() Send a DM or return its channel
client.cursor Current {after, afterId} polling cursor
client.destroy() Stop polling

HTTP endpoints

Base: https://lflkpziiwnoamvtrbcil.supabase.co/functions/v1/chat-api. Authenticate with Authorization: Bot YOUR_TOKEN.

Method Path
GET /v1/me
GET /v1/channels
GET /v1/events?after=ISO&after_id=ID
GET, POST /v1/channels/{id}/messages
PATCH, DELETE /v1/messages/{id}
GET /v1/users/{id}
POST /v1/dms
POST /v1/moderation
POST /v1/automod
DELETE /v1/automod/{id}

Message JSON uses text, embeds, and optional reply_to. The SDK maps content to text. DM JSON uses user_id. Moderation uses user_id, action, reason, optional expires_at (ISO date), and evidence.

Verification & root tools

Sign-in, registration, password recovery, human moderation, and bot creation/token reset/revocation use hCaptcha. The widget uses the site’s theme. Tokens are verified by Supabase Auth or the chat-api Edge Function; client-side checks alone never authorize moderation.

Owners configure HCAPTCHA_SECRET in Supabase Edge Functions Secrets. In Authentication Bot and Abuse Protection, enable CAPTCHA, choose hCaptcha, and save the same secret. Only the public sitekey belongs in the frontend. Complete that Auth setting after deploying the frontend.

From 20 October 2026, 00:00 Hong Kong time, human chat write operations also require a server-verified session lasting 15 minutes. All networks, including VPNs, must verify. The server checks the date and session; changing your computer clock, skipping anti-vpn.js, or using the old console override does not authorize protected operations. Bots continue to authenticate with scoped bot tokens.

GitHub Pages serves public static files. Its page overlay can be skipped by a modified browser; private data and protected chat operations remain guarded on Supabase. hCaptcha decides whether to show an interactive challenge based on the sitekey settings and visitor risk; passive mode does not guarantee a visible puzzle.

Root account management

Root can open Server settings Members to reset another member’s password or permanently delete their account. Password fields remain masked, and current passwords are never returned. Account deletion requires typing DELETE username and completing hCaptcha. Root accounts cannot be deleted or reset through these controls.

Deletion removes the login, profile, uploads, messages, moderation history, votes, polls, and owned bots with their scripts and messages. Shared channels and other members’ messages stay. External sites’ copies, exports, and provider backups are outside this operation. If storage or authentication deletion fails, keep the dialog open and retry to finish the saved job.

08

Errors & compatibility

The API allows 60 requests/minute per bot and 30 message mutations/minute. Moderation is limited to 10 actions/minute. Slowmode applies unless the bot has Manage channel permission. Polling consumes API requests.

JavaScript 
try {
  await channel.send('Hello');
} catch (error) {
  if (error.status === 429) {
    console.log('Wait', error.retryAfter || 60, 'seconds before retrying.');
  } else if (error.blocked) {
    console.log('AutoMod:', error.message);
  } else {
    console.error(error.message);
  }
}

401: invalid/revoked token. 403: permission or validation failure. 422: AutoMod blocked the message. 429: rate limit or slowmode. Sends are not retried automatically, preventing accidental duplicates.

Store client.cursor outside the process for restart recovery, then pass it to new Client({cursor}). Message handlers should be idempotent. A failed handler is reported through the error event and the cursor advances; queue durable work yourself if retries are required.

Compatibility: chatbox.js is a small SDK for this CHATBOX server, with familiar Discord-style methods. It is not discord.js and cannot connect to Discord. It does not claim complete Discord feature parity. The older chatbox-bot.mjs helper remains supported.
